nodes.avoid_direction: Avoid making risky all-in commitments or neglecting scouting. Do not assume the opponent is passive just because no units are seen.
nodes.decision_direction: Maintain current development path while keeping safety checks active. Prioritize economy and expansion, but be ready to adjust if scouting reveals aggression.
nodes.exit_or_recheck_condition: Re-evaluate when you spot the opponent's first combat unit or when you complete your second base. If the opponent shows early pressure, switch to defensive production.
nodes.next_state_summary: Continue developing with safety checks, moving into the early-midgame with more information.
nodes.opponent_situation: Enemy Intelligence shows no reliable combat-unit cues. The opponent's production and technology are light or uncertain. They could be going for an early expand, a tech rush, or a timing attack.
nodes.own_situation: Your economy, production, and technology are all light or uncertain. You have no confirmed combat units yet. Focus on establishing a solid foundation.
nodes.strategic_reason: Early game is about maximizing economy and flexibility. Overcommitting to a specific plan without information can be punished. Maintaining a balanced approach allows adaptation.
nodes.title: Early Game Development with Safety Checks
nodes.transition_goal: Reach a stable economy with at least two bases and a basic defensive structure (e.g., spine crawlers) before transitioning to more specific strategies.
nodes.trigger_summary: At the start of the game, both sides are in early game with limited information. The opponent's posture is unknown, and your own posture is also uncertain.

nodes.avoid_direction: Avoid over-investing in economy without any military. Do not ignore the possibility of a two-base all-in.
nodes.decision_direction: Maintain current development path, but start to prepare for potential aggression. Consider adding a few defensive units or scouting overlords to gain information.
nodes.exit_or_recheck_condition: Re-evaluate when you see the opponent's army composition or when you reach a certain supply. If the opponent is passive, you can continue to expand.
nodes.next_state_summary: Continue developing, but be ready to adapt if the opponent shows signs of aggression.
nodes.opponent_situation: Enemy Intelligence still shows no reliable combat-unit cues. The opponent could be teching, expanding, or preparing a timing attack. Their production and technology are light or uncertain.
nodes.own_situation: Your economy and production are still light or uncertain, but you may have a second base and some basic units. Continue to focus on macro.
nodes.strategic_reason: As the game enters the midgame, the opponent's plan becomes more critical. Maintaining economy while preparing for defense is a safe approach.
nodes.title: Early-Midgame Development with Safety Checks
nodes.transition_goal: Establish a solid economy with at least three bases and a modest army to defend against early pushes.
nodes.trigger_summary: The game progresses to early-midgame. The opponent's posture remains unknown, but you have had time to expand and develop.

nodes.avoid_direction: Avoid staying on a purely economic build without any military. Do not neglect scouting for tech structures or expansions.
nodes.decision_direction: Maintain current development path, but start to transition into a more specific strategy based on your scouting. Consider teching to a midgame composition.
nodes.exit_or_recheck_condition: Re-evaluate when you see the opponent's main army or tech structures. If the opponent is passive, you can take a fourth base.
nodes.next_state_summary: Continue developing, but be ready to commit to a specific strategy.
nodes.opponent_situation: Enemy Intelligence still shows no reliable combat-unit cues. The opponent could be hiding a tech switch or preparing a large army. Their production and technology are light or uncertain.
nodes.own_situation: Your economy and production are still light or uncertain, but you likely have multiple bases and a decent army. You need to decide whether to tech up or mass units.
nodes.strategic_reason: In the midgame, you need to have a plan. Without information, it's best to stay flexible and avoid committing to a composition that could be countered.
nodes.title: Midgame Development with Safety Checks
nodes.transition_goal: Have a solid economy and a midgame army composition that can handle common Terran strategies.
nodes.trigger_summary: The game reaches the midgame. The opponent's posture is still unknown, but you have had time to build a strong economy.

nodes.avoid_direction: Avoid being too passive and letting the opponent take a fourth base uncontested. Do not over-commit to a push without scouting.
nodes.decision_direction: Maintain current development path, but start to consider aggressive options. If you have a supply advantage, you might want to push.
nodes.exit_or_recheck_condition: Re-evaluate when you see the opponent's army composition or when you reach max supply. If the opponent is passive, you can take a fourth base.
nodes.next_state_summary: Continue developing, but be ready to commit to a decisive action.
nodes.opponent_situation: Enemy Intelligence still shows no reliable combat-unit cues. The opponent could be preparing a massive army or a tech switch. Their production and technology are light or uncertain.
nodes.own_situation: Your economy and production are still light or uncertain, but you likely have a large army and multiple bases. You need to decide whether to push or continue teching.
nodes.strategic_reason: In the late-midgame, you need to start applying pressure or you will fall behind. Without information, it's best to keep your army mobile and ready to respond.
nodes.title: Late-Midgame Development with Safety Checks
nodes.transition_goal: Have a strong army and be ready to transition into a late-game composition or a timing attack.
nodes.trigger_summary: The game enters the late-midgame. The opponent's posture is still unknown, but you have a strong economy and army.

nodes.avoid_direction: Avoid neglecting anti-ground defenses. Do not assume the opponent will stay on the ground; they might tech to air later.
nodes.decision_direction: Maintain current development path, but start to strengthen your ground army. Consider teching to units that counter Marines and Reapers, such as Banelings or Roaches.
nodes.exit_or_recheck_condition: Re-evaluate when you see more of the opponent's army composition or if they expand. If they are passive, you can continue to expand.
nodes.next_state_summary: Continue developing, but with a focus on ground defense.
nodes.opponent_situation: Enemy Intelligence shows a ground posture with representative cues like Marine and Reaper. Production and technology are heavy, and they may be planning a timing attack.
nodes.own_situation: Your economy and production are light or uncertain. You need to respond to the opponent's ground-heavy approach.
nodes.strategic_reason: The opponent is committing to a ground army. You need to prepare a ground defense and potentially a counter-attack.
nodes.title: Early-Midgame Ground Macro Response
nodes.transition_goal: Have a solid ground army and defensive structures to hold off any early pushes.
nodes.trigger_summary: The opponent shows a ground-based macro posture with heavy production and technology, possibly with Marines and Reapers. Your own posture is still unknown.

nodes.avoid_direction: Avoid focusing only on ground defense. Do not ignore the possibility of a Battlecruiser push.
nodes.decision_direction: Maintain current development path, but start to prepare for both ground and air threats. Consider teching to units like Hydralisks or Mutalisks.
nodes.exit_or_recheck_condition: Re-evaluate when you see the opponent's main army composition. If they are going for Battlecruisers, you need anti-air.
nodes.next_state_summary: Continue developing, but with a focus on a balanced army.
nodes.opponent_situation: Enemy Intelligence shows a ground posture with representative cues like Reaper and Battlecruiser. Production and technology are heavy, and they may be transitioning to air.
nodes.own_situation: Your economy and production are light or uncertain. You need to respond to the opponent's ground-heavy approach, but also be aware of potential air threats.
nodes.strategic_reason: The opponent has a mix of ground and air units. You need a balanced army to counter both.
nodes.title: Midgame Ground Macro Response
nodes.transition_goal: Have a versatile army that can handle both ground and air threats.
nodes.trigger_summary: The opponent shows a ground-based macro posture with heavy production and technology, possibly with Reapers and Battlecruisers. Your own posture is still unknown.

nodes.avoid_direction: Avoid falling behind in economy. Do not neglect scouting for tech switches.
nodes.decision_direction: Strengthen your ground army and continue to increase your economy. Consider teching to units that counter Marines, such as Banelings or Roaches.
nodes.exit_or_recheck_condition: Re-evaluate when you see the opponent's army composition or if they expand. If they are passive, you can take a fourth base.
nodes.next_state_summary: Continue developing, but with a focus on ground superiority.

nodes.own_situation: You have a ground-oriented army with moderate production and heavy expansion. You are in a good position to match the opponent's ground game.
nodes.strategic_reason: You are both going for a ground-based macro game. You need to out-produce and out-tech your opponent.
nodes.title: Early-Midgame Ground Macro with Own Ground Posture

nodes.trigger_summary: The opponent shows a ground-based macro posture with heavy production and technology, possibly with Marines. Your own posture is ground-oriented with moderate production.

opening.strategic_goal: Develop a economy / expansion / ground posture while preserving flexibility for live observation-driven adaptation.
